raw_case_text:
A 41-year-old HIV-1-infected male farmer presented with a five-day history of right hypochondriac abdominal pain associated with decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, and two days of yellowish discolouration of sclera, with no history of fever, diarrhoea, blurring of vision, and odynophagia or dysphagia.
He presented to us for the first time in September 2016, when he was diagnosed with pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonitis (PJP) on transbronchial lung biopsy and successfully treated with co-trimoxazole and prednisolone. This biopsy did not reveal CMV inclusion bodies. His CD4 count was 109/muL and HIV-1 viral load was 4.89 log copies/ml.
He was diagnosed with HIV-1 infection in 2000 and was treated by another physician, for which he was initiated on zidovudine (ZDV)/lamivudine (3TC)/nevirapine (NVP) and switched to tenofovir disproxil fumarate (TDF)/3TC/atazanavir/ritonavir (ATV/r) in 2011 due to virological failure. After control of PJP, we switched his HAART to raltegravir (RAL)/darunavir (DRV)/r based on the genotypic resistance report. Within 4 weeks of initiating HAART, he presented with the above mentioned symptoms.
Physical examination was unremarkable except for icterus and tender hepatomegaly. Fundoscopy did not reveal CMV retinitis. He had normocytic normochromic anaemia (Hb: 10.7 g/dl), normal total leucocyte, and differential counts. Liver enzymes were total bilirubin: 9.2 mg/dl (reference value: 0-1 mg/dl), aspartate transaminase (AST): 109 U/L [15-37 U/L], alanine transaminase (ALT): 41 U/L (14-59 U/L), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP): 906 U/L (46-116 U/L). Tests for hepatitis B and hepatitis C were negative.
Hepatomegaly (liver span-18 cm) with grade I-II intrahepatic biliary dilatation with focal parenchymal lesion was seen on abdominal ultrasound. The common bile duct (CBD) was dilated, measuring 14 mm suggestive of possible obstruction at the level of ampulla with no definitive mass or obstructive lesion.
An endoscopic retrograde cholangio-pancreatography (ERCP) was performed, which revealed oedematous papilla with stenosis. Cholangiogram showed a dilated CBD with prepapillary CBD stricture. All these features were suggestive of AIDS cholangiopathy (Figure 1(a)).
Wide papillotomy was performed, and a 7 Fr CBD stent was placed for biliary drainage. Bile aspirate was negative for Cryptosporidium, Microsporidium, Cyclospora, and Mycobacterium. Brush cytology of the stricture revealed inflammatory cells, pigment-laden macrophages, and several red blood cells with no acid-fast organisms.
Histopathological examination of ampullary biopsy showed focal ulcerations with superficial mucosal necrosis and acute and chronic inflammation in the mucosa and lamina propria. Cells of submucosal Brunner's glands showed nucleomegaly with eosinophilic intranuclear and basophilic cytoplasmic CMV inclusions (Figure 1(b)).
After intervention, the patient had immediate symptomatic relief and did not receive any anti-CMV treatment. Liver enzymes normalised 2 weeks later.
After 6 months, CD4 improved to 363 cells/muL with HIV viral load of 423 copies/ml. Repeat ERCP revealed normal cholangiogram with no residual stricture in lower CBD, with normal papilla (Figure 2(a)). Previously placed stent had migrated out. Cells from ampullary biopsies did not reveal intranuclear/cytoplasmic CMV inclusions (Figure 2(b)).
A repeat viral load after 8 months was <50 copies/ml. ART was switched to dolutegravir (DTG)/DRV/r.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 41-year-old HIV-1-infected male farmer with recent biopsy-proven Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia presented 4 weeks after switching salvage antiretroviral therapy with a 5-day history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting, and a 2-day history of scleral icterus.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV-1 in 2000 (previously failing ZDV/3TC/NVP and TDF/3TC/ATV/r), the patient had initially presented to our center in September 2016 with transbronchial biopsy-proven Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonitis (PJP; baseline CD4 count 109/μL, HIV-1 viral load 4.89 log copies/mL, no CMV inclusions on lung biopsy), which was successfully treated with co-trimoxazole and prednisolone. Following PJP control, his antiretroviral regimen was switched to genotype-guided salvage therapy with raltegravir and ritonavir-boosted darunavir (RAL + DRV/r). Within 4 weeks of starting RAL + DRV/r, he developed 5 days of right hypochondriac pain, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting, followed by 2 days of jaundice.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-1 infection diagnosed in 2000 with prior virological failure; recent transbronchial biopsy-proven Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonitis (September 2016) successfully treated with co-trimoxazole and prednisolone. Occupation: Farmer.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right hypochondriac abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and scleral icterus; negative for fever, diarrhea, blurred vision, odynophagia, or dysphagia. Home medications included raltegravir, darunavir/ritonavir, and co-trimoxazole.

objective.physical_examination: Scleral icterus and tender hepatomegaly (liver span 18 cm); normal fundoscopic examination without CMV retinitis; remainder of physical exam unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory tests: Normocytic normochromic anemia (hemoglobin 10.7 g/dL) with normal total and differential leukocyte counts; cholestatic liver derangement with total bilirubin 9.2 mg/dL (reference: 0–1 mg/dL), AST 109 U/L (15–37 U/L), ALT 41 U/L (14–59 U/L), and markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) at 906 U/L (46–116 U/L); negative hepatitis B and hepatitis C serologies. Abdominal ultrasound: Hepatomegaly (18 cm span), grade I–II intrahepatic biliary radicle dilatation, focal hepatic parenchymal lesion, and dilated common bile duct (14 mm) to the level of the ampulla.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline and follow-up CD4/viral load: Pre-ART CD4 count 109/μL and HIV-1 viral load 4.89 log copies/mL (improving at 6 months to CD4 363/μL and viral load 423 copies/mL, and <50 copies/mL at 8 months). Prior transbronchial lung biopsy (September 2016): Confirmed Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonitis without CMV inclusion bodies. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), bile aspiration, and ampullary biopsy: Edematous stenotic major duodenal papilla with a 14 mm dilated CBD and distal prepapillary CBD stricture compatible with AIDS cholangiopathy; bile aspirate and brush cytology negative for Cryptosporidium, Microsporidium, Cyclospora, and Mycobacterium; ampullary biopsy histopathology demonstrated focal mucosal ulceration/necrosis and enlarged submucosal Brunner's gland cells containing characteristic eosinophilic intranuclear ('owl's eye') and basophilic cytoplasmic cytomegalovirus (CMV) inclusions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Cytomegalovirus (CMV)-induced AIDS cholangiopathy (papillary stenosis and distal CBD stricture confirmed by ERCP and pathognomonic intranuclear/cytoplasmic CMV inclusions in ampullary Brunner's glands) presenting as unmasking immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) 4 weeks after initiating raltegravir plus darunavir/ritonavir in a patient recently treated for biopsy-proven Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Plan and clinical course: Treated with endoscopic wide biliary sphincterotomy (papillotomy), 7 Fr common bile duct stent placement, and continuation of antiretroviral therapy without specific anti-CMV antivirals. He experienced immediate pain relief, normalization of liver enzymes within 2 weeks, and complete resolution of the biliary stricture and histological clearance of CMV inclusions on repeat ERCP at 6 months (with CD4 rising to 363/μL).
